turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on in, Mr. Harlan. I'll grab a set of vitals before Dr. Shah sees you. Have a seat.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Sure, sure. That parking lot is a maze, I went around twice, and Carol had a hair appointment so I drove myself. Don't get me started on the construction on Maple.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one thirty-eight over eighty-four. Pulse is seventy-six. You're satting ninety-seven percent, and respirations are sixteen.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): One thirty-eight, huh. That's not terrible for me. My neighbor Ed swears by beet juice and he traps me at the mailbox every morning.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Your wife called the front desk this morning. She said you've had a tight chest for three weeks and you've been short of breath with it.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, she did not need to do that. I am not short of breath. I'm sixty-four, I'm just here for a check-up, I haven't been in for a while. She worries, you know how she is.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): I'll let the doctor know. Did you take any medicines this morning?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I took my blood pressure pill with my coffee. Skipped breakfast, though. The diner on Fifth was packed and their pancakes are huge, like ridiculous.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mr. Harlan, I'm Dr. Shah. What brings you in today?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Just a check-up, doc. It's been, what, a year? The waiting room looks different, new chairs, and my back likes these better already.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Shortness of breath?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Like I told her, I breathe fine.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Can you climb a flight of stairs?

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, um, the stairs at the house, if I go up them normal, or if I walk fast to catch the bus, I get this tight feeling in my chest. Not every single time. But yeah.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Where exactly?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Right across the chest. It's not a pain, I wouldn't call it a pain. More like a band squeezing, and then I start thinking about my grandson's soccer, he's six, and I lose the thought.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does it happen at rest?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Sitting watching the game, I'm fine. It was a blowout last Sunday, I don't even want to talk about it.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does it ease if you stop?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, if I slow down it lets up. Maybe a minute or two.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pain down the arm or into the jaw?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Nope.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sweating or nausea with it?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, neither.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cough? Fever?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough, no fever. I did have a cold around Thanksgiving but that cleared up. My sister-in-law brought this green bean thing, way too much onion.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has the tightness been there?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): A couple of months, I guess. I can't pin the day. Carol keeps saying three weeks, but she wasn't paying attention at the start.
[SEG0031] person_1 (NURSE): She was pretty definite on the phone. Three weeks.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, she's wrong. It's been at least a couple of months, longer than three weeks. And I am not breathless, I don't care what she told you.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): So weeks to a couple of months, not nailed down. Any history of heart disease?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No. High blood pressure, that's the one. They started me on a pill five-ish years ago.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Diabetes?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any surgeries?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. Not even my tonsils, and everybody had those out when I was a kid.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Name and dose of the blood pressure pill?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Lisinopril, twenty milligrams I think, maybe, I'm not a hundred percent sure, the bottle's on the kitchen windowsill. I take it once a day.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): And aspirin?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, the baby one, eighty-one milligrams. I'm supposed to take it every day, but it's on and off, when I remember.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): So you miss doses?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh yeah. Some weeks I hit most days, some weeks the bottle just sits there. My daughter got me one of those pill boxes with the days on it and I still walk past it.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any other medicines?
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I bought fish oil once and it tasted like the harbor, so that lasted a week, and I'm not taking it.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines or anything else?
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any old cholesterol or heart tests?
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Last year, at that health fair in the church basement, they said my cholesterol was borderline. No number I remember. They didn't give me a pill for it.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?

[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): I quit about fifteen years back. Was about a pack a day when I was carrying mail. Thirty-two years at the post office, retired now, thank God, and those dogs on Elm Street had it in for me.
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): A beer on Sunday with the game. That's about it.
[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm going to listen to your heart and lungs.
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Heart rhythm is regular, I don't hear a murmur. Lungs are clear. No swelling at the ankles.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Good, because these shoes are new and I didn't want them looking puffy. Got them on sale at the outlet, and Carol said they were ugly.

[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): The tightness with stairs and fast walking could be angina, it could be you're just out of shape, or it could be reflux. I am not going to say you have a blocked artery. Not today.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Angina, that's the heart one, right? My uncle had something, but he was eighty and he ate bacon every morning, so.
[SEG0060] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's one possibility on the list. I won't conclude anything until we have tests.
[SEG0061] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm ordering an ECG today and bloodwork, cholesterol, a blood count, and kidney tests, because you're on lisinopril for your blood pressure.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Needles, great. I look away, just so you know. Last time the lady couldn't find a vein and we both suffered.
[SEG0063] person_1 (NURSE): I can run the ECG in the next room when you're done, and the lab down the hall will draw the bloods.
[SEG0064] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the ECG and the labs don't explain it, we might send you for a stress test. Not booking that now.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): Like on a treadmill? I can walk, I just don't like going fast. There's a difference.
[SEG0066] person_3 (DOCTOR): Take the aspirin every day, not just when you remember. Keep taking the lisinopril once a day.
[SEG0067] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright, alright. I'll put the bottle by the coffee so I see it. Coffee I never forget.
[SEG0068] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the tightness starts while you're sitting still, or you get sweaty or sick to your stomach with it, go to the ER. Don't wait for me.
[SEG0069] person_2 (PATIENT): The ER. Got it. I don't want to go, but got it.
[SEG0070] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in two weeks and we'll go over the ECG and the labs.
[SEG0071] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. Is that a morning thing? Afternoons I watch my grandson sometimes, his mom works at the bank.
[SEG0072] person_3 (DOCTOR): The front desk will set the time. Anything else hurting?
[SEG0073] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I'm good. Well, my knee clicks on the stairs, but that's old news, not why I came. It doesn't hurt really.
[SEG0074] person_1 (NURSE): I'll walk you over to the ECG room whenever you're ready.

spec.situation: Man or woman 50-70 who comes 'for a check-up' and only slowly admits a tight feeling in the chest when climbing stairs or walking fast; first denies chest pain, later describes the tightness. Takes a BP tablet and aspirin on and off. Doctor orders ECG and bloods.
features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

bad.reason: Lisinopril, once daily, for BP, about five years supported; 20 mg is uncertain: patient said 'I think, maybe.'
bad.text: lisinopril (dose=20 mg, frequency=once daily, duration=approximately 5 years, indication=high blood pressure, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Completed borderline cholesterol check at health fair supported; not requested by patient.
bad.text: Cholesterol test (type=laboratory, status=completed, requested_by=patient, indication=health fair screening; result described as borderline)

omissions.text: Negative finding missing: the patient explicitly denied chest pain ('No. No chest pain.').
Chest symptom characterization missing/wrong: the patient said the sensation is 'not a pain' but a band-like squeezing/tightness right across the chest.
